title: A doomsday scenario for American AI - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: In a Free Press column, Cowen sketches a doomsday scenario in which AI-doom fears cause America to cede AI leadership to China, leaving Americans dependent on Chinese AI-invented drugs and devices and producing an 'invisible graveyard' of millions; he argues problem-solving beats speculative doom debate.

themes.theme: Cost of ceding AI lead to China

insights.claim: If America cedes AI leadership, sick and elderly Americans would turn to Chinese companies for AI-invented and AI-tested drugs and medical devices, paying high prices while China prioritizes its own citizens.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: AI-driven biotech leadership is a strategic asset; losing it shifts pharma value capture to China.
insights.quote: Sick and elderly Americans will go to Chinese companies for their AI-invented and AI-tested medical devices and drugs.
insights.locator: Sick and elderly Americans will go

insights.claim: Lost AI-driven medical innovation would create an 'invisible graveyard' of premature American deaths that could swell into the many millions.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Frames AI regulation costs in mortality terms, a powerful argument against restrictive policy.
insights.quote: Over time, this invisible graveyard will swell into the many millions.
insights.locator: Sick and elderly Americans will go

insights.claim: AI doom fears are not based on peer-reviewed research showing a high chance of doom, nor are they indicated in market prices including measures of risk.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Markets are not pricing AI catastrophe; Cowen treats that as evidence against doom narratives.
insights.quote: nor was doom indicated in any market prices of the time, including measures of risk

insights.claim: Slowing America's AI lead does not avert doom because destructive AI could just as well come from Chinese models.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Supports the case for US AI acceleration and against unilateral restraint.
insights.quote: the doomer scenario can come from Chinese AI as well

insights.claim: Successful societies build capability to face existential risks by solving problems incrementally, while speculative ex ante doom debate tends to demoralize and immobilize.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Signals pro-acceleration policy stance among influential economists.
insights.quote: Debating the chances of our doom, ex ante, on a highly speculative basis, is unlikely to provide the same kind of expertise and talent cultivation.
